newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian internal credits 13.9 pct up in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Romanian internal credits 13.9 pct up in Feb.

text.p: Romania's domestic credits rose by 13.9 percent to 41.9 trillion lei in February after January's 16 percent increase on the back of a surge in hard currency loans, central bank (BNR) data showed on Monday.
Net credits to government remained almost flat at 4.5 trillion lei in February, when non-government loans grew by 16.1 percent due to the upswing of hard currency loans.
Hard currency credits jumped to 20.55 trillion lei in February from 15.2 trillion lei the previous month, taking about 55 percent of end-February non-government loans.
Local bankers said the sharp rise of hard currency loans over the past months was triggered by higher lending rates on leu credits, which in February fell by about one percent.
Romanian lending rates are currently near 160 percent, compared with around 55 percent earlier this year, spurred by a central bank move to tighten monetary policy.
Short-term loans accounted for 83 percent of end-February leu loans of 16.79 trillion lei, of which state companies held 55.5 percent.
Inflation was 18.8 percent in February, with the year-on- year rate at 105.4 percent.
